comparisons.peer_topic: Deposit balance trends and drivers for 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Average deposits increased in 2024 compared to 2023 due to growth in CIB (driven by Payments and structured notes) and AWM (higher-yielding products offset by migration), while CCB declined due to increased spending; period-end deposits similarly rose in CIB and AWM but fell in CCB.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase disclose trends in average deposits, but with divergent results. Citi reports a 2% increase in average deposits, noting a partial offset from shifting to higher-yielding investments. JPMorgan also reports an increase in average deposits, driven by growth in CIB and AWM, but explicitly highlights 'migration into higher-yielding investments' as a headwind in CCB that was offset by new accounts. Both companies identify the competition from higher-yielding investment products as a factor influencing deposit balances, though Citi focuses on platform shifts while JPMorgan focuses on segment-specific migration.

sentences.text: Average deposits increased 2%, reflecting the transfers of relationships and the associated deposits from USPB ($17 billion at the time of transfer over the last 12 months), partially offset by a shift in deposits to higher-yielding investments on Citi's platform.
Average deposits increased for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, reflecting:

• an increase in CIB due to net inflows predominantly in Payments and net issuances of structured notes as a result of client demand in Markets, partially offset by deposit attrition, which included actions taken to reduce certain deposits,

• a decline in CCB primarily driven by a decrease in balances in existing accounts due to increased customer spending and migration into higher-yielding investments, predominantly offset by new accounts.
